title: Overnight IDF Airstrikes Hit Nuseirat and Bureij Refugee Camps; Dozens Injured in Central Gaza
detail: Israeli airstrikes struck the Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps in central Gaza Strip overnight on May 22–23, 2026 (Day 955 of the Gaza war), injuring dozens of Palestinians and causing heavy destruction across residential areas. Video footage from the scene showed widespread rubble and rescue teams working through the night. Both camps in central Gaza's deir al-Balah governorate have been repeatedly struck since the renewed military campaign began on May 11. The overnight strikes continued the pattern of near-daily bombardment targeting central Gaza. Cumulative Palestinian death toll since October 7, 2023 stands at 73,800+.

media.caption: Overnight Israeli strikes on Gaza — heavy destruction in Nuseirat and Bureij camps, May 23, 2026

title: IDF Airstrike on Hamas Police Post in Northern Gaza Kills 5 Officers; Weapons Depots Destroyed in Central Gaza
detail: On Day 955 of the Gaza war (May 23, 2026), an Israeli airstrike hit a Hamas police post in northern Gaza, killing at least 5 police officers and wounding additional personnel. According to Hamas, two missiles were fired at the post. An IDF spokesperson confirmed the strike targeted Hamas operatives conducting security operations. Separately, the IDF reported destroying three Hamas weapons storage facilities in central Gaza the same day; the warehouses were found to contain anti-tank missiles, firearms, RPGs, combat vests, and ammunition. Secondary explosions confirmed weapons were present at the depots. The IDF said it was continuing its campaign to degrade Hamas military capacity rebuilt during the 212-day ceasefire.

media.caption: IDF strikes Hamas police post in northern Gaza; 5 officers killed — May 23, 2026

title: France Bans National Security Minister Ben-Gvir from French Territory Over Flotilla Activist Treatment
detail: French Foreign Affairs Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced on May 23, 2026 (Day 955) an immediate travel ban barring Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir from entering all French territory. The ban was imposed citing Ben-Gvir's 'reprehensible actions' toward detained flotilla activists, referring to his posting of footage showing bound and kneeling activists at Ashdod Port following the interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla on May 18–19. France joined a growing bloc of European nations taking punitive diplomatic steps against Israel: Italy had called for EU-level sanctions discussions against Ben-Gvir, multiple European countries had summoned Israeli ambassadors, and Turkey had recalled its ambassador from Tel Aviv following the deportation of 422 flotilla activists on May 22. Ben-Gvir remained in his government post as a key coalition partner despite growing international pressure on Prime Minister Netanyahu to dismiss him.

media.caption: France bans Israeli minister Ben-Gvir from French territory — May 23, 2026
